question: What does the OptionTypeInfo verification field (record+0xac) decide?  Pin the gate in the per-entry apply 0x60bedc0 and the per-entry serializer 0x60bb9a0: which verification values skip, which error each parse failure reports, and how the 214 mapped entries distribute.

record_fields.offset: record+0x0 (i64, signed) -- field offset into the options struct
record_fields.type: record+0xa8 (i32) -- OptionType enum, 0..24; jump table at 0x9786b4
record_fields.flags: record+0xb0 (i32) -- bit flags; the type-21/22 arm tests bits 0x2/0x4/0x8 of the high byte

early_return_verification_4.outcome: Status OK written to the out-param at 0x60bf000 (movl $0x0,(%rdi); mov %si,0x4(%rdi); movq $0x0,0x8(%rdi)); the value is never parsed and the options struct is untouched
early_return_verification_4.note: verification 4 is checked BEFORE the type dispatch, so it short-circuits every type

parse_dispatch.mechanism: type jump table at 0x9786b4 (relative int32 entries); each arm calls its type-specific parse helper on (options_base + record->offset, value)
parse_dispatch.success: helper returns nonzero -> 0x60bf287 writes Status OK to the out-param and returns

type_21_22.outcome: types 21/22 fall to the 0x60bf1e0 arm, which re-attempts the parse via 0x60b9d70 and 0x6099e70 (the string at 0x445245 is the find needle); the arm's exact error outcome is NOT pinned by this item

verification_1_2_3.instruction: mov 0xac(%rbp),%eax; sub $0x1,%eax; cmp $0x2,%eax; fall through to 0x60bf09c
verification_1_2_3.outcome: Status code 3 (kNotSupported), message = 'Deserializing the option ' + <name> + ' is not supported' (built at 0x60bf09c..0x60bf1bd from the literals at 0x4373e9 (25 bytes) and 0x437403 (17 bytes), passed to the Status ctor 0x61cf670 with code 3)
verification_1_2_3.note: verifications 1, 2 and 3 are INDISTINGUISHABLE in the binary: one range check covers all three and they share the single path

verification_0_5.instruction: same range check; ja 0x60bf460 for any value outside {1,2,3} (after the verification-4 early return)
verification_0_5.outcome: Status code 4 (kInvalidArgument), message = 'Error parsing:' + <name> (the two slices at 0x60bf460..0x60bf49d: the literal at 0x4477ed (14 bytes) and the name, passed to the Status ctor 0x61cf670 with code 4)
verification_0_5.note: verification 0 and 5 share the path; any other value would too, but only 0..5 occur in the mapped entries

verification_4_skip.outcome: the option is skipped in the dump: 0x60bbae8 writes Status OK to the out-param and returns; nothing is emitted for the entry
verification_4_skip.note: the skip is checked right after the null-value guard (r8 == 0 -> 0x60bbae8), before the serialize-function/type dispatch

serialize.other_verifications: verifications 0, 1, 2, 3 and 5 all serialize normally: the record's serialize function at record+0x38 if non-null (call *0x40(%r13) at 0x60bba1b), else the type dispatch at 0x60bba28 (types 21/22/22 handled at 0x60bbbf0/0x60bbb78)

messages.not_supported: Deserializing the option <name> is not supported

open_unknowns: The exact error outcome of the type-21/22 fallback arm at 0x60bf1e0 (parse via 0x60b9d70 and 0x6099e70) when its own parse fails: the arm is cited, not modelled.
The C++ enum names for the verification values 0..5: the binary pins the behavior per value, not the source names.
Whether the type-21/22 arm is a fallback after a failed primary parse or the primary parse for those types (the jump table's 21/22 entries are not separately resolved).
The serializer's type-21/22/22 arms at 0x60bbbf0 and 0x60bbb78 are cited, not modelled.
